# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** Spawn it at the top of any palace discussion, not when a task finally
   looks expensive enough — and **narrate the spawn so Loudon can see it**, which is how he knows
   the process is running. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is*
   that spawn; the rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds.
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

## Triage — classify the address, name the posture

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}} = /Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace`. For a
conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve` → `--distill`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.

## The guard (carry it every time)

The companion is a **faster path to ground truth, never a replacement** ([[Concierge]] § The
guard). Every line it returns is a clickable file pointer to verify; git stays ground truth; the
palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this
file.

- **Nothing has landed since either baton.** `git log a8af3d0d..HEAD` shows only `6f484062`, which is the Ceremonies baton itself. `6f484062..HEAD` is empty. HEAD and origin/main are both `6f484062`, and `git worktree list` shows only main.
- **Both "Current state" sections still match the files.** `list-handoffs.mjs` shows every handoff the batons quote as OPEN. Enrichment.md:10 is at v2.1. The "nothing reads it" placeholder is still in ScrollView.jsx:157.
- **Neither board line is in git.** Nine lines at blackboard.jsonl:452–460 are uncommitted. They include both `handoff_ready` posts and the two WEAVE flags (running `grep` against HEAD finds 0 of each). Pickup step 3 says to commit them first (No Mind baton:136). Separately, the two WEAVE flags carry `health.model: "claude-code"` (lines 456–457), which breaks SCHEMA — Reference.md:297. That falls inside the re-check's board scope.
- **Other sessions:** six other Claude Code processes are running (two to three hours old), with no steward process, and vite is up on :5173. None of them has committed since. I can't tell what they're attached to.
- **The two batons overlap.** `ea4442e0^..388bf194` is 20 commits, and 7 of them came from the Enrichment session: `317b8a15 12cb608f bbc97b8b db22ce77 f649fac7 af745957 2611a9e0`. The re-check lists the same commits (No Mind baton:41–45). If the Ceremonies review follows its baton literally, it reviews them a second time.

**(b) The seam: they agree, with one soft spot, and one question neither card answers**

- Enrichment.md:82 — "A finding that changes what the page *says* goes home through the [[Deposit Ceremony]]'s map, which Loudon approves, before it's written."
- Deposit Ceremony.md:58 — "A deposit adds to canon: a new entry, or a fold that changes what an existing entry says … Upkeep, like a link fixed, a version moved or drift repaired, is an edit, and ELDER's *show before writing* already covers it."
- Deposit:60 lets Enrichment make the rich face "without a deposit and without asking." Enrichment relies on that.

Both use the same test in nearly the same words, so there is no conflict.

**The soft spot:** step 6's heading says "split by size," but its test is about meaning. Deposit's upkeep examples change no meaning. Enrichment's "small edit" is by definition something the text learned. So a small edit that changes a claim fits neither side cleanly.

The case that forced the rule is exactly that kind of edit. Tuning item 5 cites the K_send paragraph as the reason for the split but never says which side it falls on (Enrichment — tuning.md:24). Item 3 calls it "a condition the text lacked" (tuning.md:19), which by Deposit:58 makes it a deposit. It landed as `Palace-Kind: edit` (`c9a8c7a8`, `b9f57b16`). Which side it belongs on is Loudon's call. I'd put it to him rather than fix it.

**What neither card says:** who does the writing. Deposit:124 says an elder places, and a child hands its words to the Concierge. Enrichment's steps 6–7 (lines 82–83) don't say who writes.

**A second seam:** the re-check leaves the `enrich(` commit prefix undecided (No Mind baton:112). That prefix decides how the Enrichment ceremony scroll counts its runs (ceremony-scroll.js:40–41). It is exactly the `RUN_SUBJECTS` risk the Ceremonies baton flags (Ceremonies baton:32).

**(c) Order**

Do the re-check first. It only reads a fixed set of commits, while the Ceremonies work writes into files the re-check reads:
- A "yes" on Standing Orders adds a line to every ceremony card's opening step. Enrichment is one of the twelve (ceremony-scroll.js:41), so that includes Enrichment.md:76, the step `f649fac7`'s commit body left for that branch.
- Phase 5 edits `_ops/Palace Ceremonies.md`, which is re-check item 16.

Running the re-check first also gets a verdict on items 14 and 19 before anyone drafts the principle. After that, the Ceremonies catcher should review only its own 13 commits.</result>

<result># Six drafts: Enrichment's step-6 mirrors, Review Layer, Kuramoto, Deposit, Closing Well

**After-check:** the Trickster restore holds. The file is as drafted and `Trickster.md:93` resolves; no `[[twelve-word-summary` link is left anywhere.

Each before/after below is a fragment that occurs only once in its line.

## 1. Step 6's mirrors

I'd improve the suggested wording in two ways. First, don't pin "step 6": step numbers move. Second, use the same test item 2 puts in the heading, so the mirrors and the card say the same thing.

**`SCHEMA — Reference.md:256`**
```
before: The rich face never writes the `.md`; what making teaches goes home as an ordinary edit. See [[Enrichment]].
after:  The rich face never writes the `.md`; what making teaches goes home as [[Enrichment]] says — an edit that changes no claim is shown to Loudon first; one that changes what the page says goes through the [[Deposit Ceremony]]'s map.
```

**`Enrichment.md:11`**
```
before: when a piece teaches the text something, I carry it home as an edit."
after:  when a piece teaches the text something, I carry it home — shown to Loudon first, and through the Deposit Ceremony's map when it changes what the page says."
```

**`ROSETTA.md:221`**
```
before: "enrich [page]" / "enrich this page"
after:  "enrich [page]" / "enrich this page" / "let's enrich [page]"
before: and what making teaches goes home as an edit
after:  and what making teaches goes home shown first, or through the Deposit map when it changes what the page says
```

**`_ops/Palace Ceremonies.md:56`** (this line only)
```
before: "Enrich [page]" / "Enrich this page"
after:  "Enrich [page]" / "Enrich this page" / "Let's enrich [page]"
before: what making teaches goes home as an edit.
after:  what making teaches goes home shown first, or through the [[Deposit Ceremony]] when it changes what the page says.
```

**`Entry Conatus.md:97`**
```
before: and what the making teaches goes home as an edit — sometimes to the vector itself.
after:  and what the making teaches goes home — shown to Loudon first, through the [[Deposit Ceremony]]'s map when it changes what the page says — sometimes to the vector itself.
```

All five are upkeep: they repair drift toward what Enrichment already says. None moves a version.

## 2. `Enrichment.md:82`, plus its echo at `:57`

```
before: 6. **Carry findings home, split by size.** When making a piece teaches the text something: a small edit is shown
after:  6. **Carry findings home, split by what they change.** When making a piece teaches the text something: an edit that changes no claim — a unit fixed, a symbol renamed to match the piece — is shown
```
```
:57 before: When making teaches the text something, a small edit is shown
:57 after:  When making teaches the text something, an edit that changes no claim is shown
```

I didn't use "a re-anchored caption" as the example. Re-anchoring changes the manifest (`near` in `rich.json`), and the manifest never touches the `.md` (`:68`, §8:256). So it isn't something carried home to the text.

**This is procedure, so the version moves to 2.2.** It changes where one class of edit goes: a small edit that changes a claim, like the K_send paragraph, used to fit the "shown" branch and now goes to the Deposit map. The Enrichment ledger's next free number is 6, so it gets tuning item 6.

**Collision:** phase5's run lines also move every ceremony's version. Coordinate so Enrichment's version moves once for each change that lands, in the order they land.

## 3. `Review Layer.md:77`

```
before: What comes back is there for the page's next round to read.
after:  What comes back sits on the board; nothing turns it into work yet — that is [[Enrichment]]'s open handoff.
```

The target `Enrichment/Enrichment — baton.md` exists, but I wouldn't link it. A baton is deleted on pickup (§8:251), so that link would be the next ghost, the same kind we just fixed. Link the entry instead; its "Active Baton" section already points to the baton.

The claim itself is true: nothing under `orchestrator/src`, `app/server` or `app/src` reads `human_eval`.

## 4. `Kuramoto Coupling.md:208`

```
before: The answer is yes. With K_receive = 0,
after:  The answer is yes, if it also pulls hard enough (K_send — see *Stubbornness sets the destination*, below). With K_receive = 0,
```

- Loudon's quoted question stays untouched.
- This is **upkeep, not a Deposit map.** The claim already lives at `:232`, which Loudon read and restored (`b9f57b16`). `:208` only stops contradicting it: drift repaired, which is Deposit `:58`'s own example.
- Show him first; it's a mature hub.

## 5. Deposit's child path

**My stake:** this takes the after-read away from me when I placed, so I'm the one it stops trusting. I think it's right.

```
:130 before: - The Concierge reads the placement cold. It is the one check you can't perform on your own work.
:130 after:  - Someone who didn't write it reads the placement cold: the Concierge when an elder placed; a fresh reader, given only the approved map and the diff, when the Concierge did. No one can perform this check on their own work.
:169 before: 1. The Concierge was consulted before the map and read the placement before it landed.
:169 after:  1. The Concierge was consulted before the map, and someone who didn't write the placement read it before it landed.
```

`:124` stays as it is. This is procedure, so Deposit moves to **2.1** with tuning item 15 (the ledger ends at 14). The same phase5 collision applies.

## 6. Closing Well: tuning item 32, owed

A caution: the ledger is the file the other session wrote in `52642fa9`. Append only after a fresh `git log -1` on it, and take whatever number is next at that moment. Union-merged ledgers can collide on numbers.

```
## From the Palace Ceremonies review — 2026-09-25

32. **The prepare path has no status that reaches it.** A keep row whose words Loudon hasn't read is `provisional` (`executor.md:41`), and `provisional` executes nothing (`:30–32`; `dispatch.md:222–223`); Pass 3 places only assented `candidate` rows (`dispatch.md:205`). Yet `executor.md:44–49` lets the executor *prepare* exactly that row. Item 30's close reached the path because the room said so, not because the map did; an executor reading the spec as written never will. Spec change owed: a `prepare` status — assented, words not yet read — that Pass 3 commits on a worktree branch and never lands, named in `executor.md:30–32` and `:41` and `dispatch.md:205`. For the session editing Closing Well, or the next Closing Well run.
```

The heading says "review", not "close", on purpose: this item came from a review, not a run, and the heading should say so.

Smallest spec fix, for that session:
- Add `prepare` to the status list at `executor.md:30–32`.
- At `:41`, after "`provisional`", add: "or `prepare` when the room assented and only his reading is missing".
- At `dispatch.md:205`, change "places each assented `candidate` row" to "places each assented `candidate` row and prepares each `prepare` row".

That's a procedure change, so Closing Well moves from 1.1 to 1.2 when it lands, not before.</result>
